summary: This codebase follows a layered architecture with a clear separation of concerns, where the API layer handles HTTP requests and responses, the Business Logic layer orchestrates core workflows, and the Data & Storage layer manages persistence. All layers depend on Shared & Config for utilities and configuration, while Business Logic interacts with External Services and both API and Data & Storage layers, forming a bidirectional flow between API and Business Logic, and between API and Data & Storage. Tests validate interactions across multiple layers, ensuring integration fidelity.

root.label: Architecture
root.description: This codebase follows a layered architecture with a clear separation of concerns, where the API layer handles HTTP requests and responses, the Business Logic layer orchestrates core workflows, and the Data & Storage layer manages persistence. All layers depend on Shared & Config for utilities and configuration, while Business Logic interacts with External Services and both API and Data & Storage layers, forming a bidirectional flow between API and Business Logic, and between API and Data & Storage. Tests validate interactions across multiple layers, ensuring integration fidelity.

children.label: API
children.description: The API component exposes HTTP endpoints for external clients, routing requests to respective features (GitHub, user, AI) via versioned routers and handling errors uniformly.
children.insight: Entry point is src/main.py with FastAPI app, cleanly separating routers by feature under src/features/.

children.label: features
children.description: The features component organizes domain-specific API logic for GitHub, user, and AI services, each with dedicated routers and schemas to handle request routing and data validation. It acts as the primary entry point for API endpoints, abstracting business logic from the core API layer.

children.label: api
children.description: The API component exposes HTTP endpoints via a versioned router (v1_router.py) that delegates requests to business logic in the features layer, using common utilities for shared functionality like authentication and error handling. It serves as the sole entry point for external HTTP interactions.

children.label: common
children.description: The common component provides shared routing logic and centralized error handling for the API layer, ensuring consistent request processing and error responses across all endpoints.

children.label: Business Logic
children.description: The Business Logic component orchestrates domain-specific operations for GitHub repository analysis and AI-driven flow discovery, serving as the core engine that processes code structure, dependencies, and call graphs to generate actionable insights for the API layer.
children.insight: Tight coupling between dependency_parser.py, call_graph_extractor.py, and symbol_extractor.py suggests a fragile separation of concerns, despite their individual service files.

children.label: features
children.description: The features component encapsulates business logic for GitHub repository analysis and AI-driven flow discovery, handling dependency parsing, symbol extraction, and call graph generation via dedicated services.
children.insight: Clean separation: Each service is focused on a single responsibility (e.g., dependency_parser, call_graph_extractor), with no god file.

children.label: github
children.description: The github component analyzes code repositories by extracting symbols, dependencies, and architectural flows using specialized services, enabling deep codebase understanding and structure mapping.

children.label: ai
children.description: The ai component handles AI-driven workflows by orchestrating story generation and discovery processes through dedicated services, serving as a self-contained module for intelligent feature logic.

children.label: Data & Storage
children.description: This component manages all data storage and persistence layers, including database schema migrations, ORM models, and session handling, serving as the single source of truth for application data. It enables structured data access for API and Business Logic layers while abstracting database complexity.
children.insight: tight coupling between migrations/versions and models in src/features, making schema changes reliant on precise ordering and manual coordination.

children.label: migrations
children.description: The migrations component manages database schema changes over time through versioned migration scripts, ensuring the database evolves consistently with the application's data model in the src module.

children.label: src
children.description: The src component handles data persistence and database abstraction for GitHub and User features, defining models, repository interfaces, and session management. It serves as the central data storage layer, decoupling domain logic from database implementation.

children.label: External Services
children.description: The External Services component in src/features/ai/bedrock.py handles communication with Amazon Bedrock AI models, abstracting API calls and responses to provide a unified interface for the Business Logic layer.
children.insight: Entry point: all AI model interactions funnel through bedrock.py, making it a clean abstraction layer.

children.label: Infrastructure & Tooling
children.description: This component manages the full infrastructure and tooling stack, including containerized development environments, infrastructure-as-code via Terraform modules, build automation with Makefile and Poetry, and deployment configurations for multiple environments.
children.insight: Tight coupling between Terraform modules and Docker configurations suggests a shared deployment context that could benefit from clearer environment isolation.

children.label: terraform
children.description: This component manages AWS infrastructure as code using Terraform, providing reusable modules for core services like Lambda, IAM, DynamoDB, and AppSync, enabling consistent and automated provisioning of backend resources.

children.label: modules
children.description: This component consists of reusable Terraform modules that provision AWS infrastructure services such as Lambda, IAM, DynamoDB, AppSync, and others, enabling modular and consistent infrastructure deployment across environments.

children.label: appsync
children.description: This component provisions an AWS AppSync API by generating a GraphQL schema, resolvers, and VTL templates from an OpenAPI specification, automating the integration of RESTful endpoints into a GraphQL layer.
children.insight: generate-from-openapi.js is the entry point that drives the entire pipeline, orchestrating schema generation and resolver creation.

children.label: ses
children.description: The SES component manages Amazon Simple Email Service resources, including IAM permissions for email sending via a dedicated IAM module, and provides a template for user invitation emails.
children.insight: Clean separation between SES resource configuration and IAM permissions, with the latter in a dedicated subdirectory.

children.label: lambda
children.description: The lambda component defines an AWS Lambda function powered by a Python script (s3_to_celery.py) that processes S3 events and triggers Celery tasks. It encapsulates the Lambda configuration, input variables, and output exports in a reusable module.

children.label: iam
children.description: The iam component defines and manages AWS IAM resources such as roles, policies, and users, providing a reusable module for identity and access management across environments. It acts as a clean abstraction layer for IAM configurations without direct dependencies or consumers at this level.

children.label: acm
children.description: This component manages AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificates, enabling the provisioning and validation of SSL/TLS certificates for use in AWS services. It serves as a reusable module for certificate requests with domain validation options.

children.label: dynamodb
children.description: This component manages an Amazon DynamoDB table with configurable attributes, billing mode, and indexing via Terraform, serving as a reusable module for persistent key-value storage across services.

children.label: elasticache
children.description: This component manages an AWS ElastiCache Redis cluster, defining its configuration, security, and networking traits via Terraform. It serves as a reusable module for provisioning cache instances with consistent settings across environments.

children.label: security_groups
children.description: This component defines and manages AWS security groups, encapsulating inbound and outbound rule configurations in a reusable module. It serves as the single source of truth for network access policies across environments.

children.label: alb
children.description: The alb component defines an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with associated target groups and listeners, abstracting AWS ALB configuration into a reusable module. It serves as a neutral network gateway for routing HTTP/HTTPS traffic to backend services.

children.label: ebs_volumes
children.description: This component manages the creation and configuration of AWS EBS volumes, abstracting volume parameters like size, type, and encryption into reusable Terraform modules. It serves as a standardized entry point for provisioning persistent storage across different environments.

children.label: ssm
children.description: The SSM module manages AWS Systems Manager parameters and associations, providing a reusable abstraction for storing and retrieving configuration data securely via Parameter Store.

children.label: other
children.description: This component contains reusable Terraform modules for fundamental AWS infrastructure services such as VPC, EC2, S3, RDS, Secrets Manager, Route53, SQS, SNS, and Cognito, enabling consistent, parameterized deployment of core cloud resources across environments.

children.label: envs
children.description: The envs component manages separate Terraform environments (prod, dev, staging) with isolated configuration, state, and scripts for each, ensuring environment-specific infrastructure provisioning.

children.label: dev
children.description: The dev component sets up and manages the development environment using Terraform, including infrastructure provisioning and environment cleanup via custom scripts. It serves as a self-contained configuration for isolated dev workflows.
children.insight: entry point is main.tf with backend.tf and variables.tf defining core configuration and state management

children.label: prod
children.description: The prod component defines the production environment configuration for Terraform, including backend settings, variables, and main infrastructure definitions. It serves as the isolated, finalized deployment target for production workloads.

children.label: staging
children.description: The staging component defines the infrastructure configuration for the staging environment using Terraform, with dedicated variables, backend settings, and state management to ensure isolated and reproducible deployments. It serves as a staging ground for testing changes before production rollout.

children.label: scripts
children.description: This component provides templated startup scripts for EC2 instances across different environments (dev, staging, production), enabling consistent initialization of instances with environment-specific configurations.

children.label: nginx
children.description: Nginx serves as a reverse proxy and web server, managing incoming HTTP requests and routing them based on configured rules in default.conf, while nginx.conf sets core server parameters. It is a standalone component that provides network-level traffic handling without external dependencies.

children.label: docker
children.description: This component packages the application into a Docker container using a dedicated Dockerfile and entrypoint script, ensuring consistent deployment across environments.

children.label: scripts
children.description: The scripts component provides two utilities for environment management: pull-staging-env.py syncs staging environment configs, and verify-toolchain.sh ensures development toolchain dependencies are installed and valid.

children.label: Shared & Config
children.description: This component centralizes configuration management, authentication logic, and shared utilities such as logging and middleware, serving as the foundational layer for configuration consistency and security across all other components.
children.insight: tight coupling between auth/jwt.py and utils/jwt_verifier.py creates a fragile dependency for token validation logic

children.label: config
children.description: This component manages environment-specific configuration settings and logging rules, providing a structured way to load and override settings across development, staging, and production environments.

children.label: utils
children.description: The utils component provides foundational utilities for authentication, logging, and JWT verification, serving as a shared resource layer for configuration-driven operations within the application.

children.label: middleware
children.description: The middleware component handles cross-cutting concerns such as user context attachment, CORS policy enforcement, rate limiting, and request logging, acting as an infrastructure layer between incoming requests and application logic.

children.label: auth
children.description: The auth component handles authentication and authorization logic using JWT validation and AWS Cognito integration, serving as the central authority for user identity and permission checks. It provides secure, token-based access control for the application's middleware layer.

children.label: common
children.description: The common component provides centralized exception definitions and initialization logic for the application, serving as a foundational layer for consistent error handling across modules. It acts as a namespace for shared exceptions without introducing external dependencies.

children.label: Tests
children.description: The Tests component provides the testing infrastructure for the application, leveraging pytest fixtures and configurations to validate interactions with Shared & Config, Data & Storage, and API modules. It serves as the single entry point for all unit and integration tests.
